statement.p: Christina is conducting market research on the cost of homeowners insurance. Christina has determined that the average annual cost of homeowners insurance is 982, and that the distribution of costs is normally distributed with a standard deviation of 74.
a. Find the probability that a single randomly selected consumer spends more than 877 on homeowners insurance.
b. The cost of the middle 40 of homeowners insurance policies falls between (round to the nearest dollar):
c. The most expensive 20 of homeowners insurance policies cost at least how much annually?

solution.p: Define the normal distribution in Desmos: \displaystyle\text{normaldist}{\left({982},{74}\right)}.
a. In Desmos, select RIGHT region, compute AREA. Enter the boundary 877 and obtain the probability: \displaystyle{P}{\left({x}\geq{877}\right)}={0.922}.

b. For the middle 40 of the data, select INNER region, compute BOUNDS. Enter the area of the middle region \displaystyle{0.40} and obtain the upper and lower bounds: \displaystyle{943}\leq{x}\leq{1021} .
Alternatively (old Desmos approach): split the remaining region between the tails and find the boundaries:

c. For the most expensive 20 of the distribution, need \displaystyle{0.2} of the area to the right. Use a RIGHT region, compute BOUNDS and enter the area to the right \displaystyle{0.2}. Obtain the lower bound: \displaystyle{x}={1044}.
